context: The original problem f(n) moves n disks, stacked smallest on top and largest on the bottom, from source peg A to destination peg C. The figure uses five disks. Each move transfers one top disk, and a larger disk can never sit on a smaller one.
At the top level, A is the source, B is the auxiliary peg, and C is the destination. Their roles change in recursive subproblems.
description: The left side summarizes the full five-disk transfer from A to C. The right side shows three stages from top to bottom. First move the top n−1 smaller disks from A to B using C. Then move the largest disk from A to C, the one-disk subproblem f(1). Finally, use A to move the n−1 smaller disks from B onto the largest disk on C.

The first and last subproblems must themselves be broken into legal one-disk moves. The smaller stack cannot move all at once. Dashed outlines mark positions before a transfer, and solid colors mark positions after the stage. All positions refer to the same five disks.
The table gives each stage’s transfer, auxiliary peg, and final arrangement on all three pegs.

frames.explanation: The required order of the three tasks gives the move-count recurrence T(n) = 2T(n−1) + 1, which is not labeled in the figure. The first and last subproblems have the same size but different source, auxiliary, and destination roles.
frames.title: Three stages of the Tower of Hanoi

summary: Moving n disks from A to C splits into three ordered subproblems: move n−1 disks from A to B, the largest disk from A to C, then n−1 disks from B to C.
